General.Description:
When glaciologist Sigrid Haas surfaces from a collapsed research station on the Arctic ice cap with a survival kit rated for seventy-two hours and no way to call for help, she begins walking. Over the next twenty-two days, she will cover three hundred and forty kilometres of drifting sea ice to reach the nearest settlement.

Bjorn Halvorsen's film is a near-silent achievement — a survival story told primarily through landscape, physical performance, and the voice-over of Sigrid's field notes, read by Eva Lindqvist with the matter-of-fact precision of someone describing weather observations rather than the outer limit of human endurance. Lindqvist won the International Film Prize for her performance, and it is deserved: she finds enormous inner life in a role that offers almost no dialogue and constant physical demand.

Shot entirely on location in Svalbard over eighteen weeks, Arctic Drift is as cold and beautiful and ruthlessly honest as the book that inspired it. One of the finest survival films ever made.
